purpose: Replace three modern-brown-bear-like Arctodus simus gallery images with a consistent fossil-led compact-back, deep-rostrum body plan while preserving separate representative, variation-review, and ecology-review gates.
workflow: Fresh prompt-to-image candidates, original-size anatomy rejection, targeted edit of the best body-plan candidate, then anatomy-reference-guided fresh S2 and S3 compositions
license: Original project-generated bitmaps. Only factual papers and public museum specimen records supplied constraints; no external artwork, copyrighted reconstruction, franchise frame, or named-artist style was used as a generation input.

intermediateReference.prompt: Wide 16:9 museum paleoart reconstruction, original and copyright-safe, no text. Show ONE adult Arctodus simus, an extinct Pleistocene giant short-faced tremarctine bear, in full-body side/three-quarter view walking to the right across open North American steppe. This must NOT have the silhouette of any living Ursus bear. ANATOMICAL SILHOUETTE MUST BE OBVIOUS: a very short, compact torso from shoulder to hip; straight nearly horizontal topline with no grizzly shoulder hump; deep chest but a lifted, slightly tucked underside behind the ribs, not a long hanging belly; hips close behind the ribcage; robust but visibly tall limbs with long exposed forearms and lower legs, giving more ground clearance than a brown bear while remaining heavy and plantigrade, never greyhound-thin; all four legs clearly separate and straight enough to read; huge five-toed plantigrade paws with heels down. Head: very large, high rounded cranial vault, small rounded ears, exceptionally deep and broad muzzle with a short nasal bridge; the snout looks vertically deep and blunt, not long and tapered, but it is not pug-flat. Neck is powerful but does not merge into a hump. Short tail. Use short-to-medium charcoal-umber fur closely following the body contour so anatomy remains visible, with only subtle lighter muzzle shading. Calm alert posture, mouth closed, head slightly turned toward viewer. Animal occupies 45% of a wide landscape frame; entire ears, tail, four paws and breathing room visible. Low shrubs, distant conifers and mountains give scale. Reject living-bear traits: NO grizzly hump, NO rounded long low pear-shaped torso, NO sagging belly, NO thick shaggy coat hiding wrists or ankles, NO long polar-bear muzzle, NO spectacled-bear mask. Also no cat/hyena/dog anatomy, no digitigrade stance, no skinny stilt legs, no saber teeth, no roar, prey, blood, extra/fused/missing limbs, cropped feet, labels, logo, watermark, signature, border, montage, or collage. Photorealistic natural-history illustration, clear anatomy, ages 5–14.

arctodus-simus-representative-v3.prompt: Edit the supplied original paleoart image. Preserve the exact wide 16:9 landscape, lighting, one-animal composition, compact straight-backed torso, separated four limbs, and calm walking pose. Change only the Arctodus simus facial proportions and paws to correct anatomy. FACE: extend the muzzle modestly forward (about 15–20%) so the face is no longer bulldog-, mastiff-, or pug-flat. Keep the rostrum exceptionally deep and broad with short nasal bones, but make it a real bear muzzle of moderate length: the nose projects clearly in front of the eyes, the top line slopes gently rather than dropping vertically, cheeks are firm and not jowly, mouth closed. Retain a large high rounded cranial vault and small rounded ears. It must look like a giant extinct tremarctine bear, not a dog and not a modern grizzly. PAWS: reduce the apparent size of every paw by about 20–25%. Replace the spread human-hand-like digits with compact heavy bear paws. Each visible paw has five short close-set toes with short dark claws, natural webbing/fur between toes, no fingers, no opposable digit. Keep the stance plantigrade with heels grounded and correct weight distribution. Make rear paws and contact shadows anatomically clear. Do not add, remove, fuse, duplicate, or crop limbs, toes, or tail. Keep short-to-medium contour-following charcoal-umber fur, no shoulder hump, no long low belly, no other animals, and no text, logo, watermark, signature, border, collage, or labels. The result must remain museum-quality photorealistic paleoart for ages 5–14 at the same 1672×941 aspect and framing.

arctodus-simus-pattern-v2.prompt: Use the supplied approved Arctodus simus image ONLY as an anatomical identity reference. Create a completely new, original 16:9 museum-paleoart composition; do not reuse its background or pose. Show the SAME extinct giant short-faced bear body plan moving LEFT through a cool Late Pleistocene aspen-and-spruce basin in a moderately elevated rear three-quarter view. Preserve exactly the reference animal's compact straight-backed torso without a grizzly shoulder hump, deep chest, clearly exposed robust limbs, high rounded cranium, deep broad moderate-length muzzle, small round ears, and short single tail. The head turns gently toward the viewer so the deep rostrum remains readable. All four legs must attach correctly and remain separated. Use a stable slow walking pause with ALL FOUR plantigrade paws touching the ground—no lifted sole. Each readable paw is compact, bear-like and five-toed with short close-set claws; no hand-like spread digits. Change the coat to a plausible smoke-gray and cool umber variation with restrained cinnamon guard hairs; fur is short-to-medium and follows the silhouette. No living species mask. The bear occupies about 42% of the wide frame, with open space in the leftward direction. Old patchy snow, damp sedges, leafless aspens, spruce, low mist and cold side light create a different environment. Do not make a modern grizzly, brown, black or polar bear; no shoulder hump, long low pear-shaped body, sagging belly, long narrow muzzle, dog face, double tail, extra tail tuft, hand, four-toed cat paw, digitigrade stance, overly long racing legs, extra/fused/missing limb, distorted feet, roar, attack, prey, blood, text, caption, logo, watermark, signature, border, split panel or collage. Copyright-safe original natural-history art for ages 5–14, exactly 1672×941 framing.

arctodus-simus-ecology-v2.prompt: Use the supplied approved Arctodus simus image ONLY as an anatomical identity reference. Create a completely new, original wide 16:9 ecological paleoart scene; do not reuse its exact pose or background. Show the SAME fossil-led extinct body plan at a Late Pleistocene North American woodland-meadow edge. One adult Arctodus simus calmly sniffs exposed roots, tubers and insect grubs beside a naturally split rotten fallen log. No paw touches or grips the log: all four plantigrade paws stay on the ground, separated and visible, to avoid hand-like anatomy. Use a left-facing front-side three-quarter view from slightly above, with the head lowered only a little so the large high rounded cranium and deep broad moderate-length muzzle remain legible. Preserve the approved reference proportions: compact straight-backed torso, no grizzly shoulder hump, deep chest, lifted underside rather than a sagging belly, robust visibly exposed limbs, compact bear paws with five close-set toes where readable, and one short tail. The bear occupies 35–40% of frame. Use a dark charcoal-umber coat with subtle tawny edges, short-to-medium fur that follows anatomy. Warm late-afternoon side light, aspens and spruce at the meadow edge, distant open steppe and low hills. Soil disturbance, roots, bark fragments and tracks are irregular and natural, never a repeated stamp pattern. The behavior is cautious omnivorous investigation, not an attack. No living grizzly/brown/black/polar bear silhouette, no rounded shoulder hump, long pear-shaped torso, shaggy leg-obscuring coat, bulldog-flat or long narrow muzzle, cat/hyena/dog anatomy, digitigrade feet, hand-like forepaw, paw on log, extra/fused/missing limbs or toes, cropped feet, roaring, blood, carcass, other large animal, human object, text, logo, watermark, signature, border, montage or collage. Copyright-safe museum-quality natural-history art for ages 5–14, exactly 1672×941 framing.
